component: Single-scope durable caller time and policy revision floors
constraints: New component selection, not an incumbent exemption: single local protected database, one bounded metadata row, offline caller-pinned policy validation, no network or hard-real-time SLA.

Explicit exclusive initialization, no implicit creation/reset, atomic read-check-write, monotonic floors and same-revision digest consistency. Storage errors and contention must not produce a success snapshot.
alternatives: SQLite with Python sqlite3 and direct pinned-policy validation.
SQLite with Rust rusqlite or .NET Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.
Atomic JSON replacement, OS locking and explicit file/directory flush handling.
Erlang DETS persistence or Mnesia transactions.
LMDB native transactions; official documentation URL unavailable during this review.
rationale: Select native SQLite transactions to implement atomic metadata updates and cooperating-process locking without a custom journal. DELETE journaling and synchronous EXTRA request database/journal/directory synchronization, subject to filesystem and hardware guarantees.

Select Python binding for exact-byte direct use of the independently checked policy API. Rust and .NET are credible native/managed alternatives but would require validator parity or IPC; no demonstrated memory/latency requirement makes that materially preferable for one row. No ranking by convenience, installed tooling or rewrite cost.

Atomic JSON needs an additional portable locking and crash-consistency protocol. DETS lacks the chosen transaction interface; Mnesia supplies transactions with a broader runtime/database model. Neither is a demonstrated improvement for this isolated local store.
limits: KEEP records selection of a new component. No alternative implementation or performance benchmark was run.

Protected local storage and a functioning SQLite VFS are assumptions; no power-loss, filesystem fault or target-hardware qualification. Restoring/deleting the entire store can roll back state and requires independently retained evidence.
No enrollment, clock trust source, federation-floor persistence, encrypted-at-rest store, execution authority or distributed consensus.
LMDB retrieval failure limits the comparison; no claim that LMDB lacks required properties.
